BiblicalUsage: The word is the name for Egypt as the hemmed-in land, the besieged place on Israel's border. Isaiah says the brooks of defence shall be emptied and dried up, Sennacherib boasts that he has dried up all the rivers of besieged places, and Micah pictures the day when men come from the fortress city even to the river.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the name is a warning in itself: Egypt looked strong and walled, but God calls it the besieged place, because no wall keeps Him out. The powers that hem God's people in are the ones He hems in.
RelatedPeople: Isaiah; King Hezekiah; Sennacherib, King of Assyria
